title: Nilpotence of a smooth connected affine group is invariant under field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $G$ be an affine $k$-group scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $G_K=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ for its scalar extension [def-pc-base-change]. A group $H$ is nilpotent if there are an integer $s\geq0$ and a descending sequence $H=H_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1$ of closed normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] such that, for every commutative algebra $A$ over its base field, $g\in H(A)$ and $h\in H_j(A)$, the commutator $ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ belongs to $H_{j+1}(A)$. Then $G$ is nilpotent if and only if $G_K$ is nilpotent. No perfectness or algebraicity hypothesis is imposed on $K/k$.

source.place: Definition 6.24 and Remark 6.25, printed p.131; Proposition 6.38, printed p.133; scalar-extension compatibility of the generated subgroup, Section 2h, Propositions 2.46–2.48, printed pp.54–55. Agent synthesis for the descending central series; not a separate corollary in Milne.

proof.text: Construct $C_0=G$ and, inductively, $C_{j+1}=[G,C_j]$ using [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-relative-commutator]. Its statement gives at each stage a smooth connected normal closed subgroup of $G$, contained in $C_j$, and containing every commutator of $G$ with $C_j$ on every $k$-algebra. The induction starts because $G$ is normal in itself. Each $C_{j+1}$ is minimal among all closed subgroups containing those commutators, with no regularity assumption on the competing subgroup.

source.place: Definition 6.24, Remark 6.25(b), p.131; descending central series preceding Proposition 6.38, p.133.

proof.text: For each $j$, put $X=G\times_kC_j$ and $c(g,h)=ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$. The affine-product lemma [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and finite-type composition/base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] make $X$ affine of finite type. The identity pair is a rational point and $c(e,e)=e$ by [def-sc-group-scheme]. Normality from [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] gives $ghg^{-1}\in C_j(R)$ and the identity $c(g,h)^{-1}=c(g^{-1},ghg^{-1})$, so the image is inversion stable for every $R$. Membership of every commutator in a closed subgroup is equivalent to factorization of $c$: test the universal point of the affine scheme $X$; its pullback kills the defining ideal, hence descends to the quotient, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus the minimality in step 1 meets exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-pointed-generated-subgroup-field-extension]. Consequently $(C_{j+1})_K$ is minimal among closed subgroups of $G_K$ containing the commutator map $G_K\times_K(C_j)_K\to G_K$. The latter map is $c_K$, since products and group operations base change functorially [def-pc-base-change, def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Propositions 2.46–2.47, pp.54–55, applied to Definition 6.24, p.131. Finite-type products: Stacks Tags 01T3 and 01T4.

proof.text: If $G=H_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1$ is a central series over $k$, base change each closed immersion using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). For every $K$-algebra $R$, the fibre-product definition [def-pc-base-change] identifies $(H_j)_K(R)=H_j(R)$ and $G_K(R)=G(R)$ with $R$ regarded as a $k$-algebra. Hence the subgroup and normality conditions of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and each commutator containment of the given series, hold for these same groups. Its endpoints are $G_K$ and $1_K$. It is therefore a nilpotent series for $G_K$.

source.place: Definition 6.34 and Remark 6.35, p.133, evaluated on extension-field algebras. Closed immersions under base change: Stacks Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Conversely let $G_K=H_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H_s=1_K$ be a nilpotent series over $K$. We prove $(C_j)_K\subseteq H_j$ for $0\leq j\leq s$. The case $j=0$ is equality. Given the inclusion at $j<s$, each commutator of $G_K(R)$ with $(C_j)_K(R)$ belongs to $H_{j+1}(R)$ for every $K$-algebra $R$. Testing on the universal point of $G_K\times_K(C_j)_K$ as in step 2 gives factorization of the commutator morphism through $H_{j+1}$. Step 2 and [lem-sfb-pointed-generated-subgroup-field-extension] give $(C_{j+1})_K\subseteq H_{j+1}$. This proves the induction. Since every subgroup contains the identity, its last inclusion gives $(C_s)_K=1_K$. The competing $H_j$ need not be smooth or connected.

source.place: Proposition 6.38, p.133, inclusion induction; Proposition 2.47, p.55, for the central terms after scalar extension.

proof.text: Write $C_s=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and let $\epsilon:B\to k$ be its identity-point homomorphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-group-scheme]. The affine-product lemma [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its scalar-extension coordinate ring with $B\otimes_kK$. Step 4 says the base-changed identity is an isomorphism, so for every $b\in B$ the element $(b-\epsilon(b)1)\otimes1$ is zero. The map $k\to K$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sfb-nonzero-field-algebra-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to the $k$-module $B$: $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ is injective. Thus $b=\epsilon(b)1$ for all $b$, and $B=k$ compatibly with its identity point. Hence $C_s=1$. Step 1 now supplies the required nilpotent series $G=C_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq C_s=1$ over $k$. For $s=0$ this same argument says $G=1$, so it also treats the zero-length case.

source.place: Proposition 6.38, p.133, final termination argument; Stacks Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective, applied over the ground field.

proof_origin.place: Synthesis of Proposition 2.47, Definition 6.24, Remark 6.25(b), Definition 6.34, Remark 6.35 and Proposition 6.38 (pp.55, 131, 133), with faithful-flat injectivity from Stacks Tag 05CK. The field-invariance assertion is not a separately stated corollary in Milne.
